# 1 Kings Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-Hiram king-of Tyre sent ʾet-his-servants to Solomon, for he-had-heard that ʾet-him they-had-anointed as-king in-place-of his-father, for Hiram had-been a-lover-of David all his-days.

**2** And-Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

**3** "You know ʾet-David my-father, that he-was-not able to-build a-house for-the-name-of YHWH his-God, because-of the-war that surrounded-him, until YHWH put-them under the-soles-of his-feet.

**4** And-now, YHWH my-God has-given-rest to-me all-around; there-is-no adversary and-no evil occurrence.

**5** And-behold, I am-saying to-build a-house for-the-name-of YHWH my-God, as YHWH spoke to David my-father, saying, 'Your-son whom I-will-set in-your-place upon your-throne — he will-build the-house for-my-name.'

**6** And-now, command that-they-cut for-me cedars from the-Lebanon. And-my-servants will-be with your-servants, and-the-wages-of your-servants I-will-give to-you according-to all that you-say. For you know that there-is-no man among-us who-knows to-cut timber like the-Sidonians."

**7** And-it-was when Hiram heard ʾet-the-words-of Solomon, and-he-rejoiced greatly, and-said, "Blessed is YHWH today, who has-given to-David a-wise son over this great people."

**8** And-Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, "I-have-heard ʾet what you-sent to-me. I will-do all your-desire concerning timber-of cedar and-timber-of cypress.

**9** My-servants will-bring-them-down from the-Lebanon to the-sea, and-I will-make-them into-rafts on-the-sea to the-place that you-send to-me, and-I-will-break-them-up there. And-you will-carry them away. And-you will-do my-desire, to-give food for-my-household."

**10** And-Hiram was-giving to-Solomon timber-of cedar and-timber-of cypress — all his-desire.

**11** And-Solomon gave to-Hiram twenty thousand cors-of wheat as-food for-his-household, and-twenty cors-of beaten oil. Thus Solomon gave to-Hiram year by-year.

**12** And-YHWH gave wisdom to-Solomon, as he-spoke to-him. And-there-was peace between Hiram and-between Solomon, and-the-two-of-them cut a-covenant.

**13** And-the-king Solomon raised a-labor-levy from-all Israel. And-the-levy was thirty thousand men.

**14** And-he-sent-them to-the-Lebanon, ten thousand in-a-month by-rotation: a-month they-would-be in-the-Lebanon, two months at-his-house. And-Adoniram was over the-levy.

**15** And-Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and-eighty thousand stone-cutters in-the-hill-country,

**16** besides Solomon's chief officers who were over the-work — three thousand three hundred who-ruled over the-people who-did the-work.

**17** And-the-king commanded, and-they-quarried great stones, costly stones, to-lay-the-foundation-of the-house with-hewn stones.

**18** And-the-builders-of Solomon and-the-builders-of Hiram and-the-Gebalites cut-them, and-they-prepared the-timber and-the-stones to-build the-house.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **5:1 — "a-lover-of David"**: Hebrew ʾohev — the term describes political alliance through the language of personal affection. Hiram's love for David was both diplomatic and genuine.

2. **5:4 — "no adversary" (אֵין שָׂטָן)**: The word satan here means simply "adversary" — the political conditions for temple-building require the absence of any opponent.

3. **5:11 — "twenty cors of beaten oil"**: Some LXX manuscripts read "twenty thousand cors." The MT's modest number may reflect the premium value of pure pressed oil versus the bulk grain payment.

4. **5:13 — "labor-levy" (מַס)**: The same word from 4:6 now applied to all Israel. The scale is staggering: 30,000 conscripts rotating in shifts, plus 150,000 laborers. This is state power at full extension.

5. **5:18 — "Gebalites"**: Craftsmen from Gebal (Byblos), a Phoenician city renowned for masonry. The temple is an international project — Israelite vision with Phoenician expertise.

— EMET
